thread:
claire: quick design question — for eval runs list, can we add inline help that appears on hover for each prompt-set row? thinking: trigger on focus/hover so keyboard users get the same affordance
oliver: yes — accessibility-first. the tooltip should be reachable via keyboard focus. maybe show on :focus-visible and on hover.
daria: +1. also we need to ensure tooltip content is concise. current copy in mock: "Why this prompt was selected / last-run metrics / regression delta". feels dense.
mike: can we avoid overflow? long tooltips -> should truncate and offer an expanded panel on Enter.
claire: good call. proposal: short summary line in tooltip + a "More details (Enter)" affordance that opens the side panel. that keeps hover small and keyboard flows intact.
oliver: keyboard shortcut thoughts — people want quick approve/reject while scanning. what about `A` to approve, `R` to reject when a row is focused? with `Shift+A` for bulk approve?
daria: careful: single-key shortcuts can conflict with browser or screen reader commands. we should use `Ctrl/Meta+A` and `Ctrl/Meta+R` for safety, and document them in the tooltip.
mike: agree with modifier keys. also we need visible focus state and announceable live region updates when action completes: e.g., "Scorecard approved, 3 remaining" for screen readers.
devx-bot: reminder — keyboard shortcuts need to be toggleable in account settings per accessibility guidelines (WCAG 2.1).
claire: noted. accessibility checklist: 1) tooltip accessible on focus/hover, 2) focus outline visible (no color-only), 3) shortcuts use modifier keys and are configurable, 4) live region updates for actions, 5) tooltip content concise + links to side panel.
oliver: UX microcopy suggestion for tooltip: "Run summary — last score: 82 (−3). Press Ctrl+Enter to open details, Ctrl+R to reject." shorter than current.
daria: tiny nit: say "Press Ctrl+Enter to open details" might clash with global submit in some contexts. prefer "Press Ctrl+O to open details" and reserve Ctrl+Enter for submit in run creation flows.
mike: hmm, we already use Ctrl+O elsewhere. maybe `Shift+Enter`? ugh. this is why we need a short mapping table and an escape hatch in settings.
claire: let's not block on exact combos — requirement is that they are with modifiers and discoverable in tooltips + settings. we can run a quick mapping doc with dev to avoid conflicts.
oliver: also check focus order: when tooltip opens with keyboard, it must not trap focus; pressing Enter should move focus into the details panel (and close tooltip). Tab should go to next interactive element in the row.
daria: accessibility QA items added to the ticket: VoiceOver + NVDA tests for tooltip, confirm live region announcements, test with high-contrast mode, test focus when opening side panel via keyboard.
mike: implementation note for eng: use `aria-describedby` to attach tooltip to the focused row and `aria-live="polite"` for the status messages. CSS: `.row:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid Highlight; }`
claire: copy tweak for approval confirm: instead of "Approve"/"Reject" use "Mark as OK" / "Mark as Problem"? this helps non-native readers.
oliver: I like the plain language idea. maybe "Accept"/"Request changes"? need to align with legal wording.
daria: let's keep it neutral and consistent with scorecards. I'll run copy variants in the next sprint's microcopy pass.
mike: small perf thing — don't render detailed metric chips until tooltip is actually opened. that avoids extra DOM for long lists. lazy-load content on first open.
claire: good. and also cache the last-opened side-panel per user so repeated opens are snappy.
oliver: visual design: tooltip should have a visible pointer and 6px padding; on mobile it should become a tap-to-expand panel not hover.
daria: mobile accessibility note: hover-tooltips don't exist there, so ensure the row has an inline "i" icon that is reachable and opens the panel.
mike: will add a small 1px squash animation for tooltip to reduce motion for users who prefer reduced-motion. obey `prefers-reduced-motion`.
claire: next steps: design to produce updated mock for desktop + mobile, add keyboard mapping doc for engineering, and add the accessibility QA checklist to the ticket. who wants to own follow-ups?
oliver: I can own the keyboard mapping doc and the design mocks.
daria: I'll take microcopy and QA checklist.
mike: I'll add the implementation notes and a quick spike for performance implications.
claire: perfect — I'll create the ticket and assign. tagging product-review in case they want to weigh in on wording: @product-review :eyes:
oliver: thanks — will post mock tomorrow afternoon. :thumbsup:
daria: thanks all — small follow-up: should we include a small "keyboard shortcuts" help modal accessible from header for discoverability?
claire: yes, add that to follow-ups. end-to-end discoverability is important.
mike: note for release: feature should be behind a feature flag for a gradual rollout and to run a small internal accessibility pilot first.
claire: thanks team — I'll drop the ticket link once created and paste the initial copy + mock attachments there.
devx-bot: ticket created: PRJ-4821 — "Inline help & keyboard flows for eval runs" (assignee: claire).
